I'll follow the cursor to read ranks 6–10.
Next I'll cross-check question 5 with a store-side aggregate of orders per customer.
Now I'll cross-check question 6 with a Cypher aggregate of units per category over non-cancelled orders.

input.statement: MATCH (l:order_line)-[:of_order]->(o:order), (l)-[:of_product]->(p:product) WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' RETURN p.category, sum(l.qty) AS units ORDER BY p.category

content.text: The refusal says aggregate groups come ordered by key already, so I'll drop the ORDER BY and retry.

input.statement: MATCH (l:order_line)-[:of_order]->(o:order), (l)-[:of_product]->(p:product) WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' RETURN p.category, sum(l.qty) AS units

content.text: I'm done reading, so I'll clear the pin I set at the start.

I pinned every read to position 74 of lake `trade`, so all the answers below come from the same state. At that position the store holds 6 customers, 4 suppliers, 11 products, 12 orders and 27 order lines, and no records are retired. I read every one of those tables in full and checked the totals and joins against the store's own aggregates and graph queries.

**1. Orders placed by Harbor Supplies (C-2)**
| Order | Date | Total | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| O-1002 | 2026-08-11 | 372.00 | shipped |
| O-1006 | 2026-09-09 | 142.50 | open |
| O-1011 | 2026-10-13 | 144.00 | cancelled |

Evidence: in `order_find`, these are the only orders whose `customer` is C-2. In `customer_find`, C-2 is Harbor Supplies.

**2. Products on order O-1007**
- P-21 Check valve DN25: 2 units (line L-1007-1)
- P-40 O-ring set: 8 units (line L-1007-2)

The units at list price add up to the order total of 181.00 (2 × 42.50 + 8 × 12.00).

**3. Suppliers of the products on order O-1004**
- Lago Valvole (S-2), Italy (IT), makes P-20 Ball valve DN25.
- Torino Guarnizioni (S-4), Italy (IT), makes P-40 O-ring set and P-41 Gasket DN25.
- Nordic Fasteners (S-1), Sweden (SE), makes P-10 Hex bolt M8.

**4. Open orders with at least one valve**
- O-1004 contains P-20.
- O-1007 contains P-21.
- O-1009 contains P-20.

The other open orders (O-1006, O-1010 and O-1012) contain only fasteners, seals or pumps.

**5. Orders per customer, all statuses**
| Customer | Orders | Total |
|---|---|---|
| Delta Metals (C-1) | 3 | 1653.00 |
| Harbor Supplies (C-2) | 3 | 658.50 |
| Brightwater Utilities (C-3) | 2 | 2611.50 |
| Kestrel Farms (C-4) | 2 | 247.00 |
| Ostrava Machining (C-5) | 2 | 1035.00 |
| Vale Hardware (C-6) | 0 | 0.00 |

The store's aggregate grouped by customer gives the same figures. Vale Hardware doesn't appear in that aggregate because it has no orders.

**6. Units ordered per category, leaving out cancelled orders (O-1005 and O-1011)**
- Fasteners: 4490
- Seals: 163
- Valves: 25
- Pumps: 14

My first query for this was refused because it sorted the groups (`ORDER BY`), which the store doesn't allow on grouped results; it returns groups in key order anyway. I dropped the sort and reran it, and the result matched my count by hand.

**7. Order lines ranked by quantity, ranks 6–10**
I read the ranking in two pages of five lines each, using the store's cursor.
| Rank | Line | Order | Product | Qty |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6 | L-1012-2 | O-1012 | P-12 | 300 |
| 7 | L-1006-2 | O-1006 | P-11 | 250 |
| 8 | L-1006-1 | O-1006 | P-10 | 200 |
| 9 | L-1004-4 | O-1004 | P-10 | 150 |
| 10 | L-1012-1 | O-1012 | P-10 | 90 |

Ranks 1–5 were 1200, 800, 700, 400 and 400. The tie at 400 sits inside ranks 4–5, so it doesn't change which lines fall in ranks 6–10.

**8. How Kestrel Farms and Ostrava Machining are connected**
Customers have no direct link to each other in the data. The shortest connection runs through a product both of them ordered:

Kestrel Farms (C-4) ← placed order O-1012 ← line L-1012-2 → **P-12 Washer M8** ← line L-1008-1 → order O-1008 → placed by Ostrava Machining (C-5)

That is 7 records in all, and P-12 is the only product they have in common. A link through a shared supplier would need more records.

**9. Products never ordered**
- P-13 Threaded rod M8 (fasteners, made by Nordic Fasteners)
- P-42 Shaft seal 30mm (seals, made by Torino Guarnizioni)

The graph query for products with no order line returns exactly these two. The full list of 27 lines also confirms it.
